title: Fix the order convention for correspondence action
as_he_states: Choose between Cy and yC and check the signs in composition.
plausible_today: Fix target-first versus source-first notation once; in an oriented graded theory use the unique Koszul signs induced by that convention.
state_of_art: Stacks45.3 verifies the ungraded cycle convention. The current four-factor argument establishes the signed extension without changing factor order; Hua2026 expressly excludes this Koszul part.
why_open: The manuscript explicitly leaves a convention choice, rather than reporting a mathematical obstruction.
worth: Worth a short editorial run because one convention table prevents several false formula comparisons.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Verify the correspondence category axioms
as_he_states: The Cartesian axiom was forgotten; associativity and units remain to verify.
plausible_today: Under projection formula and Cartesian base change, pull–multiply–push composition is associative and has diagonal identities.
state_of_art: Stacks45.3.1 and45.3.3 give the exact theorem and proof; independent proof and P¹ certificate are saved.
why_open: The pages show an unfinished verification, not a reason for abandonment.
worth: Closed; useful as a concise companion proof rather than a new research problem.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Determine the meaning of the proposed diagonal basis
as_he_states: The small-factor lists are called a base, followed later by an empty relations section.
plausible_today: Separate a universal diagram algebra, its spanning marked partitions, and the realization-dependent kernel in H*(X^r); no universal independence in every realization is true.
state_of_art: The P¹ relation Δ=h1+h2 refutes independence. Hua2026 §1 gives multiplication reduction in an ungraded algebraic model, not every realization kernel.
why_open: The source does not explain why the relations section was left blank.
worth: Worth developing as a precisely bounded presentation problem after choosing the realization and coefficient ring.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Resolve the first excess coefficient
as_he_states: The transverse case is marked OK; the next case retains χ followed by a question mark.
plausible_today: For a connected join of unmarked partitions of k factors, with nonempty block counts s,s′, the excess is TX^{⊕(k+1−s−s′)}. Its first nonzero Euler contribution is χ in cohomology.
state_of_art: Stacks42.54.4–5 and45.7.8 give the geometric inputs; Hua2026 Theorem1.1 gives the parallel ungraded multigraph formula.
why_open: Only the visible uncertainty is known; no historical motive for dropping it is supplied.
worth: Closed in cohomology; an integral Chow version should retain the actual top Chern zero-cycle.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Scope of stability after the cancelled extension
as_he_states: Stability under selected operations is proposed, while an extraordinary-pullback paragraph is cancelled.
plausible_today: Marked diagonal spans are stable under the specified coordinate operations and correspondence composition; arbitrary extraordinary maps require new hypotheses.
state_of_art: The explicit one-factor operations are checked in Hua2026 §1; the geometric argument uses Stacks45.3 and42.54. No source supports reinstating the cancellation.
why_open: Cancellation is visible, but its reason is not stated.
worth: Worth only a targeted companion clarification unless a broader class of maps is explicitly chosen.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Complete the GIT coordinate chart verification
as_he_states: The inverse-map and coordinate checks are left to the reader; physical typescript page3.5 is absent.
plausible_today: Under the R-partition frame and invertible-minor conditions, the normalization maps identify the open configuration chart with PGL×its slice.
state_of_art: Mumford GIT chapter3 verifies the construction in the opened1982 edition. The structural inverse proof is checked here; exact OCR symbol collation is not complete.
why_open: The text deliberately defers the check. The missing page is a package boundary, not evidence of an abandoned theorem.
worth: Worth an editorial collation run with the original edition, not new quotient research.
author: David Mumford

title: Complete the stability cone and greedy proof chain
as_he_states: The sorted-weight cone is used; the final greedy proof continues on an absent page, and the displayed separator omits nonzero.
plausible_today: Require a nonzero separating functional in the relevant span, then use the stated step rays and minimum-weight basis argument.
state_of_art: GIT1982 has the corresponding Proposition3.6/Corollary3.7 chain, though OCR gaps limit exact formula collation. The cone formula and greedy exchange argument are re-proved here.
why_open: The last physical page3.16 is absent; no historical abandonment is inferred.
worth: Closed mathematically; worth recovering the missing page and checking the functional qualifier on the ink.
author: David Mumford

title: Specialization and the primitive integral generator
as_he_states: The specialization arrow and parity-dependent kernel/cokernel calculations are left partly open.
plausible_today: Use the vanishing-cycle sequence for a regular ordinary smoothing; keep integral saturation separate from rational primitive cohomology, since λ maps to twice a generator in the middle quotient.
state_of_art: Deligne1974 §4.2–4.4 supplies the exact sequence. Karpenko Theorem1.10 and the saved Smith form determine the integral middle lattice.
why_open: The draft leaves arrows and a purity phrase unfinished; it gives no reason for stopping.
worth: Worth a focused integral companion calculation, particularly at2.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: When is quadric inertia genuinely nontrivial?
as_he_states: For odd n the vanishing line is said to have nontrivial inertia.
plausible_today: Require a regular ordinary quadratic smoothing, control ramification, and coefficients detecting−1; the written flat/projective hypotheses alone are insufficient.
state_of_art: Deligne1974 §§4.2–4.3 supplies the regularity and character statement. The even ramified family overC[[t]] is a complete counterexample to the unqualified claim.
why_open: The source does not discuss the ramified-base-change obstruction.
worth: Worth incorporating the explicit counterexample into the companion; the corrected local theorem is established.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Cone Gysin sign and low-degree conventions
as_he_states: The Gysin sign is ξ or−ξ; the affine comparison and local-support group formulas leave degree-zero ambiguities.
plausible_today: For E=O_X(−1)^×, use c1=−h and reduced cohomology ofE for local cohomology of the contractible cone; retain H⁰ in ordinary specialization sequences.
state_of_art: Stacks42.54.7 verifies the line-bundle input; the pair exact sequence and connectedness prove the low groups. Deligne1974 supplies the vanishing-cycle context.
why_open: The page explicitly marks the sign; no further historical explanation is present.
worth: Closed after conventions; worth a single consistent integral diagram in the companion.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Local versus compact cohomology of the contracting cone
as_he_states: H_a*(C)≃H_c*(C) is followed by double question marks.
plausible_today: For a positively contracting G_m action and a weakly equivariant constructible complex with permitted coefficients, the costalk and compact-support complexes agree.
state_of_art: Braden2003 Lemma6, with the affine-space specialization and closed pushforward, gives this precise result; its proof was read.
why_open: The source marks uncertainty but does not state an obstruction or abandonment.
worth: Closed for the equivariant cone; worthwhile to specify the functorial map and coefficients.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Finish affine-quadric middle duality and orientation
as_he_states: The induction has unfinished middle slots and an explicit warning about losing a sign.
plausible_today: Separate D=0; use U≃TS^D, Poincaré duality, and the orientation sign (−1)^{D(D−1)/2}; the middle map is0 for oddD and (−1)^{D/2}2 for evenD.
state_of_art: Deligne1974 §4.1 gives the signed self-intersection table. Karpenko Theorem1.10 fixes the integral lattice used by Gysin induction.
why_open: The proof itself remains incomplete; no external reason for dropping it is stated.
worth: Worth a convention audit and exact integral diagram, not a new computation of Betti numbers.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Interpret the punctured-cone coefficient tables
as_he_states: The displayed torsion/free degrees and the coefficient notation must agree with multiplication by the hyperplane class.
plausible_today: Use the corrected integral degrees; finite2-primary coefficients have the adjacent kernel group as well as the cokernel. Do not replace an unclear coefficient byZ orZ₂ without saying so.
state_of_art: The exact hyperplane lattice is checked in Karpenko Theorem1.10 and the saved Gysin matrices. The degree corrections follow independently.
why_open: The pages do not explain these index discrepancies.
worth: Worth prioritizing for scan review because two independent degree errors change the stated groups.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Normalize the primitive quadric class
as_he_states: The half-class, primitive square, restriction and Gysin maps are worked out with unsettled signs and indices.
plausible_today: Use ruling classes α,β, h^ν=α+β, λ=α−β; retain the index2 lattice and λ²=(−1)^νh^{2ν}.
state_of_art: Karpenko Theorem1.10 and its ruling proof give the exact integral ring. The current SNF and Q² computations independently verify the corrections.
why_open: Several source slots are amended or cancelled, but no reason for stopping is stated.
worth: Worth a concise integral basis dictionary shared across all quadric sheets.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Affineness of the maximal-torus scheme
as_he_states: Finite type is flagged for checking; affineness is promised later, with an alternative route cancelled.
plausible_today: For smooth affine finite-presentation G with locally constant reductive rank, the maximal-torus scheme is smooth and affine over the base.
state_of_art: SGA3 XII Corollary1.10 gives representability/smooth separated finite type, and Corollary5.4 supplies affineness. Both statements were read.
why_open: The text explicitly defers affineness; the cancellation does not invalidate the completed published proof.
worth: Closed; useful for reconstructing proof order and avoiding the cancelled alternative.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Containment maximality versus fibrewise maximality
as_he_states: A converse existence assertion is referred to a later exposé, with artinian or locally reductive qualifications.
plausible_today: Retain the distinction over general bases; the fibrewise comparison G⊃H⊃T uses equality of geometric reductive ranks.
state_of_art: SGA3 XII Definition1.3/Remark1.4 and Proposition1.17 give the exact distinction and forward reference. No unrestricted general-base converse is verified.
why_open: The source intentionally defers the broader existence result.
worth: Worth a short hypothesis glossary; the supplied pages do not pose an unconditional new theorem.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Repair the nested-torus Weyl comparison
as_he_states: The lemma claims W(R) is a subquotient ofW(T) for nested toriR⊂T.
plausible_today: AssumeT is a maximal torus ofG; then (N(R)∩N(T))/C(T) is a subgroup ofW(T) surjecting ontoW(R).
state_of_art: The checked SGA3 XII2.3 text retains the broad wording, but its proof uses maximality. The explicitSL4 counterexample disproves the broad statement; the refined proof is supplied here.
why_open: No authorial explanation or published erratum was found in the recorded searches.
worth: Highest-priority correction candidate because the missing hypothesis survives the checked published text.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Complete the reductive-centre proof fragments
as_he_states: The field existence proof and quotient-centre proof end abruptly; some parts and references are blank or missing.
plausible_today: Use the universal multiplicative-type centre with the precise affine-fibre and smooth connected-fibre hypotheses of SGA3 XII4.3,4.4 and4.7.
state_of_art: Those published statements and the4.7 proof through the rigidity conclusion were read. The malformed intersection and missing source parts remain documentary issues.
why_open: The pages contain drafting gaps, not a statement that the centre theorem was abandoned.
worth: Closed mathematically; worthwhile to restore exact dependency order in a companion.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: Delzant’s degree-two injectivity question
as_he_states: Is grad²Q(F)→H²(F,Z/2) injective for every field of characteristic different from2?
plausible_today: The map J²/J³→H²(F,Z/2) is an isomorphism, after identifying Delzant’s actual symbol map.
state_of_art: Milnor1970 Theorem4.1 identifies K₂^M/2 withI²/I³; Merkurjev1981 p543 identifies it withBr[2]. The J/I and symbol identifications were independently checked.
why_open: The offprint offers the question without an explanation of its difficulty; no historical motive is invented.
worth: Solved; worth including a precise map comparison so the later theorem answers exactly this question.
author: A. Delzant

title: Generate the two-torsion Brauer group by quaternion classes
as_he_states: Is every Brauer class of order2 a sum of cup products a.b?
plausible_today: For every field with2 invertible, the quaternion symbol K₂^M(F)/2→Br(F)[2] is an isomorphism.
state_of_art: Merkurjev1981 states the exact theorem; the later author’s Theorem2.2 and Stacks Kummer sequence were also read.
why_open: The offprint states the question but does not explain why it remained open then.
worth: Solved; its value here is accurate attribution and chronology.
author: A. Delzant

title: Identify the unfinished purity assertion
as_he_states: The final R^{n−1}f_* purity phrase is incomplete.
plausible_today: No unique modern theorem is identifiable until coefficients, weight normalization and extension functor are fixed.
state_of_art: Deligne1974 §4.4 and SGA7II metadata locate surrounding local theory, but do not determine the missing formulation.
why_open: Only the truncated phrase survives in the supplied passage.
worth: Worth recovering context and ink before creating a research task with a guessed statement.
author: Alexander Grothendieck

title: The reported perfect-complex λ-structure solution
as_he_states: A previously open problem is reported solved by Deligne, with the written theory limited to schemes over a field.
plausible_today: Use derived exterior-power operations with their λ identities in the verified modern scope; separate historical attribution from a claim about all ringed topoi.
state_of_art: BGMN2022 Theorem1.1 supplies polynomial functoriality on perfect categories; Köck–Zanchetta2025 compares the operations under the explicit divisorial hypotheses. SGA6 frontmatter was checked only as historical metadata.
why_open: The source reports a solution, not continued openness.
worth: Worth archival identification of Deligne’s manuscript, not relabelling a solved operation construction as an open problem.
author: Grothendieck reporting Pierre Deligne

title: Conditional Leray degeneration in the seminar report
as_he_states: Deligne proves degeneration modulo the fibre Lefschetz conjecture, with an analytic Kähler analogue mentioned.
plausible_today: A degree2 endomorphism ofRf_*Q satisfying relative hard Lefschetz gives splitting and hence Leray degeneration; the analytic application needs such a relative class.
state_of_art: Deligne1968 Proposition1.2 and Theorem1.5 give exactly the splitting criterion. Mere Kählerness of individual fibres is not silently substituted for the global operator.
why_open: The report states the condition; the final weights application is truncated.
worth: Worth merging with the main cote12 hard-Lefschetz material and recording the relative-class hypothesis.
author: Grothendieck reporting Pierre Deligne

title: Finish the affine mirror local-finiteness proof
as_he_states: The proof that a proper affine reflection group has locally finite mirrors ends mid-sentence.
plausible_today: Properness implies that only finitely many distinct reflecting hyperplanes meet a compact set.
state_of_art: The classical proper discrete setting is checked in Coxeter1934; the compact-set stabilizer argument is independently completed in proof_notes.md §7.
why_open: The supplied typescript page is cut off; this is not evidence of a mathematically open question.
worth: Closed; useful as a short completion with properness explicit.
author: Unidentified reused reflection typescript

title: The promised nonaffine extension and scheme-based structure program
as_he_states: The introduction anticipates treating Chevalley structure over an arbitrary base with advantage, promises to remove affine hypotheses in §§6–8, and asks for a complete recasting of XI/XII/XV/XVI.
plausible_today: Keep the three statements distinct: a mathematical extension with local-torus hypotheses, a broad structural program over schemes, and an editorial wish. None supplies an unrestricted theorem merely by removing the word affine.
state_of_art: SGA3 XII7.1(a,b) proves the stated nonaffine torus–Cartan and conjugacy conclusions assuming local existence. XII7.7 warns that constant reductive rank alone fails outside affine fibres. The SGA3III publisher description confirms the completed arbitrary-base reductive-group structure program; it is bibliographic scope evidence, not an audit of that whole volume.
why_open: The introduction gives a methodological preference and an editorial request, but no explanation of abandonment; the verified later work develops the program.
worth: Useful as a historical scope note, not as a newly open classification problem.
author: Alexander Grothendieck
